  "meta_commentary": "## Critical Wiring Detail (Unresolved Flag Resolution)\n\nThe single remaining open flag (`multi-select-selection-sync`) is an executor-level wiring problem. Here's the exact solution:\n\n**Hook call chain**: `useTimelineState()` \u2192 calls `useTimelineData()` \u2192 which calls `useTimelineSave(queries, provider, onSaveSuccessRef)` at line 79. Selection state (`selectedClipId`, `setSelectedClipId`) lives inside `useTimelineSave` (lines 60-65). `commitData` (lines 175-215) does selection pruning at lines 187-193.\n\n**Problem**: `useMultiSelect` can't be instantiated before `useTimelineSave` because it needs to be wired into `commitData`'s pruning logic, but `useTimelineSave` runs first.\n\n**Solution**: Ref-based bridge pattern.\n1. `useTimelineData` creates `const pruneSelectionRef = useRef<((validIds: Set<string>) => void) | null>(null)` and passes it to `useTimelineSave` as a 4th parameter.\n2. `useTimelineSave.commitData` calls `pruneSelectionRef.current?.(new Set(Object.keys(nextData.meta)))` after existing selectedClipId pruning (after line 193).\n3. `useTimelineData` exposes `pruneSelectionRef` in its return.\n4. `useTimelineState` instantiates `useMultiSelect()`, then in a `useLayoutEffect`: `dataHook.pruneSelectionRef.current = multiSelect.pruneSelection`.\n\nThis ensures pruning works on the very first render cycle after the ref is populated, and covers ALL data mutation paths (save, reload, split, realtime sync) because they all flow through `commitData`.\n\n## Execution Strategy\n\n- **Phase 1 (T1-T5)**: Foundation. Selection state + save integration + click unification + visual. This is the riskiest integration work. Verify thoroughly before proceeding.\n- **Phase 2 (T6-T7)**: Marquee. Independent of batch ops. Can be done in parallel with T8-T9.\n- **Phase 3 (T8-T9)**: Quick batch wins (delete + mute). Low risk, proves the selection model.\n- **Phase 4 (T10-T13)**: Multi-drag. Highest complexity. preferred);\n+\n+    if (distance < bestDistance) {\n+      bestDistance = distance;\n+      bestStart = candidateStart;\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  return bestStart;\n+}\n@@\n export function resolveOverlaps(\n   rows: TimelineRow[],\n   rowId: string,\n   clipId: string,\n   meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>,\n@@\n \n   return { rows: nextRows, metaPatches };\n }\n+\n+export function resolveGroupOverlaps(\n+  rows: TimelineRow[],\n+  movedClips: GroupMovedClip[],\n+  _meta: Record<string, ClipMeta>,\n+): TimelineRow[] {\n+  if (movedClips.length === 0) {\n+    return rows;\n+  }\n+\n+  const movedClipsByRow = new Map<string, GroupMovedClip[]>();\n+  for (const movedClip of movedClips) {\n+    const existing = movedClipsByRow.get(movedClip.rowId);\n+    if (existing) {\n+      existing.push(movedClip);\n+    } else {\n+      movedClipsByRow.set(movedClip.rowId, [movedClip]);\n+    }\n+  }\n+\n+  const nextRowsById = new Map<string, TimelineRow>();\n+\n+  for (const [rowId, rowMovedClips] of movedClipsByRow) {\n+    const row = rows.find((candidate) => candidate.id === rowId);\n+    if (!row) {\n+      return rows;\n+    }\n+\n+    const movedClipIds = new Set(rowMovedClips.map((clip) => clip.clipId));\n+    const movedActionsById = new Map(\n+      row.actions\n+        .filter((action) => movedClipIds.has(action.id))\n+        .map((action) => [action.id, action]),\n+    );\n+\n+    if (movedActionsById.size !== rowMovedClips.length) {\n+      return rows;\n+    }\n+\n+    const preferredStart = Math.min(...rowMovedClips.map((clip) => clip.newStart));\n+    const preferredEnd = Math.max(...rowMovedClips.map((clip) => clip.newEnd));\n+    const groupDuration = preferredEnd - preferredStart;\n+    const siblings = row.actions.filter((action) => !movedClipIds.has(action.id));\n+    const groupStart = findBestGroupStart(preferredStart, groupDuration, siblings);\n+\n+    if (groupStart === null) {\n+      return rows;\n+    }\n+\n+    const delta = groupStart - preferredStart;\n+    const movedUpdates = new Map(\n+      rowMovedClips.map((clip) => {\n+        const currentAction = movedActionsById.get(clip.clipId);\n+        if (!currentAction) {\n+          return [clip.clipId, null] as const;\n+        }\n+\n+        return [\n+          clip.clipId,\n+          {\n+            ...currentAction,\n+            start: clip.newStart + delta,\n+            end: clip.newEnd + delta,\n+          },\n+        ] as const;\n+      }),\n+    );\n+\n+    if ([...movedUpdates.values()].some((value) => value === null)) {\n+      return rows;\n+    }\n+\n+    nextRowsById.set(rowId, {\n+      ...row,\n+      actions: row.actions.map((action) => movedUpdates.get(action.id) ?? action),\n+    });\n+  }\n+\n+  return rows.map((row) => nextRowsById.get(row.id) ?? row);\n+}\n*** End Patch\n"

  "meta_commentary": "## Critical Wiring Detail (Unresolved Flag Resolution)\n\nThe single remaining open flag (`multi-select-selection-sync`) is an executor-level wiring problem. Here's the exact solution:\n\n**Hook call chain**: `useTimelineState()` \u2192 calls `useTimelineData()` \u2192 which calls `useTimelineSave(queries, provider, onSaveSuccessRef)` at line 79. Selection state (`selectedClipId`, `setSelectedClipId`) lives inside `useTimelineSave` (lines 60-65). `commitData` (lines 175-215) does selection pruning at lines 187-193.\n\n**Problem**: `useMultiSelect` can't be instantiated before `useTimelineSave` because it needs to be wired into `commitData`'s pruning logic, but `useTimelineSave` runs first.\n\n**Solution**: Ref-based bridge pattern.\n1. `useTimelineData` creates `const pruneSelectionRef = useRef<((validIds: Set<string>) => void) | null>(null)` and passes it to `useTimelineSave` as a 4th parameter.\n2. `useTimelineSave.commitData` calls `pruneSelectionRef.current?.(new Set(Object.keys(nextData.meta)))` after existing selectedClipId pruning (after line 193).\n3. `useTimelineData` exposes `pruneSelectionRef` in its return.\n4. `useTimelineState` instantiates `useMultiSelect()`, then in a `useLayoutEffect`: `dataHook.pruneSelectionRef.current = multiSelect.pruneSelection`.\n\nThis ensures pruning works on the very first render cycle after the ref is populated, and covers ALL data mutation paths (save, reload, split, realtime sync) because they all flow through `commitData`.\n\n## Execution Strategy\n\n- **Phase 1 (T1-T5)**: Foundation. Selection state + save integration + click unification + visual. This is the riskiest integration work. Verify thoroughly before proceeding.\n- **Phase 2 (T6-T7)**: Marquee. Independent of batch ops. Can be done in parallel with T8-T9.\n- **Phase 3 (T8-T9)**: Quick batch wins (delete + mute). Low risk, proves the selection model.\n- **Phase 4 (T10-T13)**: Multi-drag. Highest complexity. T12 (resolveGroupOverlaps) has no dependencies and can start early. If group overlap resolution proves too complex, use the safe fallback: reject the drop (no-op) rather than auto-resolve.\n- **Phase 5 (T14-T17)**: Polish. Bulk panel, shortcuts, context menu, realtime verification.\n\n## Key Files Quick Reference\n- `useTimelineSave.ts:175-215` \u2014 commitData with selection pruning\n- `useTimelineData.ts:73-80` \u2014 hook instantiation order\n- `useTimelineState.ts:22-26` \u2014 where useMultiSelect gets wired\n- `useClipDrag.ts:144` \u2014 pointer-down session creation\n- `useClipDrag.ts:244-274` \u2014 pointer-up selection + drop logic\n- `useClipDrag.ts:229` \u2014 cross-track vertical threshold (skip for multi-drag)\n- `resolve-overlaps.ts:75-147` \u2014 existing single-clip overlap resolution\n- `snap-edges.ts` \u2014 snapDrag function to extend with excludeClipIds\n- `ClipAction.tsx` \u2014 clip rendering + current onClick selection to remove\n- `useTimelineState.types.ts:19-68` \u2014 TimelineEditorContextValue to extend"

Selection state (`selectedClipId`, `setSelectedClipId`) lives inside `useTimelineSave` (lines 60-65). `commitData` (lines 175-215) does selection pruning at lines 187-193.\n\n**Problem**: `useMultiSelect` can't be instantiated before `useTimelineSave` because it needs to be wired into `commitData`'s pruning logic, but `useTimelineSave` runs first.\n\n**Solution**: Ref-based bridge pattern.\n1. `useTimelineData` creates `const pruneSelectionRef = useRef<((validIds: Set<string>) => void) | null>(null)` and passes it to `useTimelineSave` as a 4th parameter.\n2. `useTimelineSave.commitData` calls `pruneSelectionRef.current?.(new Set(Object.keys(nextData.meta)))` after existing selectedClipId pruning (after line 193).\n3. `useTimelineData` exposes `pruneSelectionRef` in its return.\n4. `useTimelineState` instantiates `useMultiSelect()`, then in a `useLayoutEffect`: `dataHook.pruneSelectionRef.current = multiSelect.pruneSelection`.\n\nThis ensures pruning works on the very first render cycle after the ref is populated, and covers ALL data mutation paths (save, reload, split, realtime sync) because they all flow through `commitData`.\n\n## Execution Strategy\n\n- **Phase 1 (T1-T5)**: Foundation. Selection state + save integration + click unification + visual. This is the riskiest integration work. Verify thoroughly before proceeding.\n- **Phase 2 (T6-T7)**: Marquee. Independent of batch ops.   "meta_commentary": "## Critical Wiring Detail (Unresolved Flag Resolution)\n\nThe single remaining open flag (`multi-select-selection-sync`) is an executor-level wiring problem. Here's the exact solution:\n\n**Hook call chain**: `useTimelineState()` \u2192 calls `useTimelineData()` \u2192 which calls `useTimelineSave(queries, provider, onSaveSuccessRef)` at line 79. Selection state (`selectedClipId`, `setSelectedClipId`) lives inside `useTimelineSave` (lines 60-65). `commitData` (lines 175-215) does selection pruning at lines 187-193.\n\n**Problem**: `useMultiSelect` can't be instantiated before `useTimelineSave` because it needs to be wired into `commitData`'s pruning logic, but `useTimelineSave` runs first.\n\n**Solution**: Ref-based bridge pattern.\n1. `useTimelineData` creates `const pruneSelectionRef = useRef<((validIds: Set<string>) => void) | null>(null)` and passes it to `useTimelineSave` as a 4th parameter.\n2. `useTimelineSave.commitData` calls `pruneSelectionRef.current?.(new Set(Object.keys(nextData.meta)))` after existing selectedClipId pruning (after line 193).\n3. `useTimelineData` exposes `pruneSelectionRef` in its return.\n4. `useTimelineState` instantiates `useMultiSelect()`, then in a `useLayoutEffect`: `dataHook.pruneSelectionRef.current = multiSelect.pruneSelection`.\n\nThis ensures pruning works on the very first render cycle after the ref is populated, and covers ALL data mutation paths (save, reload, split, realtime sync) because they all flow through `commitData`.\n\n## Execution Strategy\n\n- **Phase 1 (T1-T5)**: Foundation. Selection state + save integration + click unification + visual. This is the riskiest integration work. Verify thoroughly before proceeding.\n- **Phase 2 (T6-T7)**: Marquee. Independent of batch ops. Can be done in parallel with T8-T9.\n- **Phase 3 (T8-T9)**: Quick batch wins (delete + mute). Low risk, proves the selection model.\n- **Phase 4 (T10-T13)**: Multi-drag. Highest complexity. T12 (resolveGroupOverlaps) has no dependencies and can start early. If group overlap resolution proves too complex, use the safe fallback: reject the drop (no-op) rather than auto-resolve.\n- **Phase 5 (T14-T17)**: Polish. Bulk panel, shortcuts, context menu, realtime verification.\n\n## Key Files Quick Reference\n- `useTimelineSave.ts:175-215` \u2014 commitData with selection pruning\n- `useTimelineData.ts:73-80` \u2014 hook instantiation order\n- `useTimelineState.ts:22-26` \u2014 where useMultiSelect gets wired\n- `useClipDrag.ts:144` \u2014 pointer-down session creation\n- `useClipDrag.ts:244-274` \u2014 pointer-up selection + drop logic\n- `useClipDrag.ts:229` \u2014 cross-track vertical threshold (skip for multi-drag)\n- `resolve-overlaps.ts:75-147` \u2014 existing single-clip overlap resolution\n- `snap-edges.ts` \u2014 snapDrag function to extend with excludeClipIds\n- `ClipAction.tsx` \u2014 clip rendering + current onClick selection to remove\n- `useTimelineState.types.ts:19-68` \u2014 TimelineEditorContextValue to extend"
